papers.title: Graph-Theoretic Analysis of Phase Optimization Complexity in Variational Wave Functions for Heisenberg Antiferromagnets
papers.abstract: We study the computational complexity of learning the ground state phase structure of Heisenberg antiferromagnets. Representing Hilbert space as a weighted graph, the variational energy defines a weighted XY model that, for $\mathbb{Z}_2$ phases, reduces to a classical antiferromagnetic Ising model on that graph. For fixed amplitudes, reconstructing the signs of the ground state wavefunction thus reduces to a weighted Max-Cut instance. This links sign optimization of wavefunctions directly to combinatorial optimization.

papers.title: Tensor computing application programming interface: An application-oriented, lightweight API for portable high-performance tensor network computations
papers.abstract: Tensor networks (TNs) are a central computational tool in quantum science and artificial intelligence. However, the lack of a unified software interface across tensor-computing frameworks severely limits the portability of TN applications, coupling algorithmic development to specific hardware and software back ends. To address this challenge, we introduce the Tensor Computing Application Programming Interface (TCAPI)---an application-oriented, lightweight API designed to enable framework-independent, high-performance TN applications, currently specified for \texttt{C++} and \texttt{Python}. TCAPI provides well-defined type-system conventions that abstract tensor objects, together with a minimal yet expressive set of core functions for essential tensor manipulations and tensor linear-algebra operations, with operation semantics shared across language specifications. Through numerical demonstrations of representative tensor-network applications implemented in \texttt{C++} using TCAPI, we show that code written against TCAPI can be migrated seamlessly across heterogeneous hardware and software platforms while achieving performance comparable to native framework implementations. We further provide open-source implementations of TCAPI based on \textit{Cytnx} and \textit{ITensor} in \texttt{C++}, and on \textit{NumPy} in \texttt{Python}, demonstrating its practicality and ease of integration with existing tensor-computing frameworks.

papers.title: Proliferation Transitions for Quantum Doubles of Groups
papers.abstract: Proliferation transitions are phase transitions between a 2+1d topological order $\mathcal{T}$ and another $\mathcal{T}/\mathcal{A}$, obtained by condensing anyons in an algebra $\mathcal{A}\subset \mathcal{T}$. We consider such transitions in quantum doubles of groups, $\mathcal{T}=D(G, \omega)$, for finite groups $G$ possibly with three-cocycle $\omega$, for which condensable algebras are fully classified. Given a condensable algebra $\mathcal{A}$, we represent $\mathcal{T}$ in terms of a Symmetry Topological Field Theory (SymTFT), that is tailored to the $\mathcal{A}$ proliferation transition. The SymTFT bulk is constructed from the M\"uger center of the subcategory generated by the algebra, i.e. the category of transparent lines, which can be bosons or fermions. Properties of the transition can then be inferred directly from the algebra classification data. For gauged Landau-Ginzburg (LG*) type transitions, we show that they do not only depend on the anyons in $\mathcal{A}$ through their field content, but the cubic interactions are fixed in terms of the multiplication structure of $\mathcal{A}$. Applied to twin algebras, which have the same anyon content but different multiplication structures, we show that twins result in distinct proliferation transitions.

papers.title: Quantum Oscillations across Hole Crystallization in Rhombohedral Graphene
papers.abstract: Recent quantum-oscillation measurements in rhombohedral graphene reveal an abrupt increase in the dominant frequency and the emergence of additional frequencies as the carrier density is lowered toward superconductivity. Noninteracting band models can account for multiple frequencies but do not explain the upward jump. We show that these features can arise from two competing fates of the inner hole pocket in an annular Fermi sea: collapse into a simply connected Fermi liquid or crystallization into an anticrystal, in which localized holes coexist with itinerant electrons. Pocket collapse contracts the outer Fermi contour at fixed density, whereas hole crystallization preserves a larger contour that supports magnetic-breakdown orbits. This contrast provides a possible explanation for the frequency jump, while additional reconstructed orbits produce a multitone spectrum. Our results support the anticrystal as a candidate normal state near superconductivity in rhombohedral graphene.

papers.title: Luther-Emery liquid in one-dimensional attractive Fermi gas
papers.abstract: One-dimensional (1D) interacting Fermi gases underpin a rich variety of quantum liquids, ranging from the Tomonaga-Luttinger liquid and the Fulde-Ferrell-Larkin-Ovchinnikov paired state to the Luther-Emery liquid (LEL). Notably, the LEL-characterized by gapless excitations in charge or spin degree of freedom and gapped excitations in the other-has long been theoretically predicted but has eluded definitive experimental observation to date. By exactly solving the attractive Yang-Gaudin model via the Bethe ansatz, we fully determine the low-energy excitation spectra for both spin and charge channels. For fully paired fermions, the spectrum features gapped spin excitation coexisting with gapless charge excitation. We further employ bosonization to derive analytical expressions for the dynamical structure factor (DSF) of the gapped spin excitation, which is a long-standing challenge in this study. In the trapped gas, we find that the spin Bragg spectroscopy peak occurs at a much higher frequency than the charge-mode peak, where the splitting frequency between these two peaks scales approximately linearly with the interaction strength. Crucially, the spin gap manifests as a sharp threshold in the spin DSF, below which spectral weight is completely absent, proving a direct and unambiguous spectroscopic fingerprint of the LEL. Our work establishes quasi-1D trapped attractive Fermi gases as a pristine experimental platform for the long-sought direct observation of the LEL.

papers.title: Chiral magnetic excitations in the RMn6Sn6 kagome metals (R=Tb, Ho, Er, and Y)
authors: Iowa State University Department of Physics and Astronomy)
Iowa State University Department of Physics and Astronomy)
S. X. M. Riberolles (Ames National Laboratory)
Iowa State University Department of Physics and Astronomy)
D. L. Abernathy (Oak Ridge National Laboratory Neutron Scattering Division)
Rebecca L. Dally (National Institute of Standards and Technology Physical Measurement Laboratory Sensor Science Division)
J. W. Lynn (National Institute of Standards and Technology Center for Neutron Research)
Iowa State University Department of Physics and Astronomy)
papers.abstract: Recent inelastic neutron scattering (INS) investigations of the kagome metal TbMn6Sn6 reveal novel chiral magnetic excitations associated with the kagome layer. These excitations appear to have an itinerant character with a large energy scale (> 100 meV) and heavy damping; however, the origin of these excitations, which are not predicted by local moment linear spin-wave theory, is not understood. Here, we use INS to show that chiral excitations are also found in RMn6Sn6 compounds with R=Tb, Ho, Er, and Y having uniaxial, tilted, planar ferrimagnet, and planar double-spiral magnetic structures, respectively. Thus, the chiral excitations exist regardless of the magnetic structure. Additionally, R=Er and Y demonstrate that the chiral mode intensity is weaker in planar magnetic structures, suggesting that excitations are transverse to the local Mn moment direction. The chiral excitations appear only at L=odd positions in the Brilloun zone, and correspond to chiral spin exciations of the same handedness within each kagome layer, and pi out-of-phase between layers.

papers.title: Persistent Photo-Enhancement of Molecular Orbital Excitations in the Kondo Insulator FeSb$_2$
papers.abstract: When insulators are excited by photons with above-gap energies, photo-doped carriers are transiently generated. Typically, orbital excitations weaken and broaden due to increased screening by these transient carriers, followed by a few-ps recovery via phonon thermalization. Here we report the observation of anomalous dynamics of many-body molecular orbital excitations in the narrow-gap Kondo insulator FeSb$_2$. In the pumped X-ray absorption spectra following excitation with 1~$\mu$m photons, we observe a transient transfer of absorption intensity from the delocalized states at the main absorption peak to the localized molecular orbital states at the pre-edge. At the resonance of the low-energy molecular orbital excitations, the pumped resonant inelastic X-ray spectra show an approximately 30\% intensity increase at a pump fluence of 11 mJ/cm$^2$ concomitant with the emergence of an energy gain feature. While the energy gain feature disappears after about 1-2~ps, the increased molecular orbital excitation intensities partially persist for at least 50~ps with no discernible energy shift. These observations require the invocation of a many-body excitation picture beyond single particle population changes.

papers.title: Lattice symmetry breaking and strain control of single-$\mathbf{q}$ magnetism in Na$_3$Co$_2$SbO$_6$
papers.abstract: Distinguishing single-$\mathbf{q}$ from multi-$\mathbf{q}$ magnetism constrains microscopic spin Hamiltonians. Here we determine the ground state of the candidate Kitaev magnet Na$_3$Co$_2$SbO$_6$ through its coupling to the lattice. High-resolution neutron diffraction reveals a spontaneous monoclinic-to-triclinic distortion at the magnetic transition, in contrast to the absence of detectable lattice-symmetry breaking in triple-$\mathbf{q}$ Na$_2$Co$_2$TeO$_6$. Together with strain-selective magnetic responses, this identifies single-$\mathbf{q}$ order in Na$_3$Co$_2$SbO$_6$ over the proposed symmetry-preserving double-$\mathbf{q}$ state. Uniaxial compression along a low-symmetry in-plane direction achieves the domain selection that magnetic-field training could not, revealing the intrinsic field-induced phase boundaries of the dominant domain. These results establish strain as a symmetry-conjugate field for magnetic domains and highlight magnetoelastic coupling as a route to diagnose, manipulate, and potentially tune magnetic states.

papers.title: Good-$\Gamma$ Numbers: A Shell-Optimized Route to the Thermodynamic Limit in Quantum Monte Carlo Calculations of the High-Density Two-Dimensional Electron Gas
papers.abstract: Single-particle finite-size errors remain a central obstacle in quantum Monte Carlo (QMC) simulations of periodic systems, conventionally reduced via twist averaging (TA). Here we introduce Good-$\Gamma$ (GG) particle numbers as system sizes $N$ at which the $\Gamma$-point Hartree--Fock (HF) energy of the high-density two-dimensional uniform electron gas (2D UEG) lies anomalously close to its thermodynamic-limit (TL) value. All results in this work concern the 2D UEG in its high-density Fermi-liquid regime, $r_s=1$--$4$. We systematically investigate the kinetic- and exchange-energy errors, $\Delta KE(N)$ and $\Delta EX(N)$, that underlie this one-body finite-size-error cancellation across four densities and both spin polarizations. We then compare diffusion Monte Carlo (DMC) energies extrapolated to the TL from GG-$N$ sequences against twist-averaged extrapolations at the same densities and polarizations, finding agreement to within a fraction of a millihartree in every case, independent of whether a $1/N$ or an $N^{-5/4}$ extrapolation form is used.

papers.title: Thermodynamic Stability of Classical $\mathbb Z_2$ Lattice Gauge Models
papers.abstract: Finite-temperature phases are traditionally studied through spontaneous symmetry breaking, but symmetry-breaking fields can remove their distinction, as in the Ising model. This motivates the search for stable nontrivial thermal phases without symmetry protection. For classical $\mathbb Z_2$ lattice gauge models with spins on $m$-dimensional cells in a fixed spatial dimension $d$, we prove joint analyticity of the thermodynamic free-energy density in temperature and perturbation strength at sufficiently low positive temperatures under sufficiently weak local perturbations, whenever $1\le m\le d-2$. Perturbations need not preserve internal or gauge symmetries and may include noncommuting quantum interactions. A separate high-temperature expansion yields an analytic region reaching infinite temperature at any fixed finite perturbation strength. These results establish thermodynamic stability and support the conjecture that low- and high-temperature regimes remain separated by a thermal transition without symmetry protection.

papers.title: Local-Channel Stability of Classical $\mathbb Z_2$ Lattice Gauge Models
papers.abstract: We establish sufficient conditions for two-way local quantum-channel stability in classical $\mathbb Z_2$ lattice gauge models with spins on $m$-dimensional cells of a $d$-dimensional lattice. Each interaction multiplies the spins on the boundary of an $(m+1)$-cell. This family, defined on the full spin Hilbert space without a Gauss-law constraint, includes the Ising model at $m=0$ and the magnetic sector of the toric code at $m=1$. The low-temperature proof combines two ingredients: locally indistinguishable flat sectors and extended magnetic defects of dimension $d-m-1$. For $1\le m\le d-2$, sufficiently weak local classical perturbations at sufficiently low positive temperature preserve equivalence to the canonical flat ensemble. No internal or gauge symmetry is required of the perturbation. For weak noncommuting perturbations, we prove the same conclusion in a smaller sufficient window by reducing the diagonal probabilities to a weak classical interaction and recovering the coherences with a local channel. The conversion channels use product ancillary inputs, have polylogarithmic causal radius, and achieve any prescribed inverse-power whole-system trace-norm error. Sufficiently high-temperature states are instead two-way equivalent to a product state. Independent finite-dimensional onsite systems can be included with weak local couplings. An optimized covariance between two distant neighborhoods of parallel $m$-tori is nonincreasing under one-way local conversion and invariant under two-way conversion. Its values $\mathcal F_m=1$ and $0$ distinguish the proved low- and high-temperature domains without a protecting symmetry. These sufficient domains do not determine the full phase diagram.

papers.title: Direct Urca process facilitated by non-Fermi-liquid quantum criticality
papers.abstract: Conventional Fermi-liquid theories of dense nuclear matter predict that the direct Urca process requires a proton fraction above a threshold of $Y_p \approx 0.11$--$0.15$, which is rarely reached in low-mass neutron stars. Here we show that this stringent kinematic constraint is drastically relaxed by the non-Fermi liquid behavior arising from superfluid and superconducting quantum criticality in neutron stars. In the non-Fermi-liquid regimes, nucleons have a smooth momentum occupation without a sharp Fermi surface, and their chemical potentials develop a logarithmic temperature dependence. These intrinsic features fundamentally alter the standard $\beta$-equilibrium relation. Consequently, direct Urca neutrino emission can be activated even at low nuclear densities. This modifies the long-standing Urca-threshold paradigm and indicates that direct Urca process has the opportunity to occur in low-mass neutron stars.

papers.title: Rare-earth tuning of magnetic entropy and interaction scales in K$_3$$Ln$(PO$_4$)$_2$ ($Ln$ = Yb, Gd) for adiabatic demagnetization refrigeration
papers.abstract: Adiabatic demagnetization refrigeration (ADR) based on frustrated rare-earth magnets provides a promising route toward helium-free sub-Kelvin cooling, while balancing magnetic entropy and interaction scales is essential for optimizing the ADR functionalities. Here we investigate the low-temperature magnetic and ADR properties of the alkali rare-earth double phosphates K$_3$$Ln$(PO$_4$)$_2$ ($Ln$ = Yb, Gd), which crystallize in a monoclinic $P2_1/m$ structure containing distorted isosceles triangular lattices of rare-earth ions. Magnetization and specific heat measurements confirm the absence of long-range magnetic ordering down to 0.1 K in both compounds. Direct quasi-ADR measurements demonstrate strongly contrasting refrigeration behaviors: K$_3$Yb(PO$_4$)$_2$ reaches a minimum temperature of 29.8 mK from an initial state of 2 K and 6 T, whereas K$_3$Gd(PO$_4$)$_2$ exhibits extended hold times below 150 mK associated with its larger magnetic entropy reservoir. Crystal-electric-field calculations confirm a $J_{\mathrm{eff}} = 1/2$ ground-state doublet in K$_3$Yb(PO$_4$)$_2$, while thermodynamic analysis based on magnetic entropy and interaction scales accounts for the distinct ADR performance of the two compounds. These results identify K$_3$$Ln$(PO$_4$)$_2$ as a chemically robust platform for rare-earth-tunable solid-state ADR.

papers.title: Contrasting Crystal-Field and Dipolar Anisotropies in the Triangular Antiferromagnet NaBaEr(BO$_3$)$_2$
papers.abstract: The magnetic ground states of rare-earth frustrated magnets can be governed by competing energy scales arising from crystal-field anisotropy, exchange interactions, and long-range dipolar interactions. Here we investigate this interplay in the triangular-lattice antiferromagnet NaBaEr(BO$_3$)$_2$ by combining magnetization, specific heat, and neutron scattering measurements. Neutron powder diffraction resolves rotations of the ErO$_6$ octahedra and supports the lower-symmetry $R\bar{3}$ structure over the previously proposed $R\bar{3}m$ model. Magnetization measurements and inelastic neutron scattering establish an effective spin-1/2 description of its low-temperature magnetism with pronounced easy-axis anisotropy, arising from a well-isolated Kramers ground-state doublet separated from the first excited crystal-electric-field level by approximately 4 meV. Below $T_{\rm N}=0.1$ K, single-crystal neutron diffraction reveals A-type antiferromagnetic order with the ordered moment predominantly oriented within the $ab$ plane, despite the pronounced paramagnetic easy-axis anisotropy. The estimated dipolar interaction scale is comparable to $T_{\rm N}$, and classical dipolar-energy calculations for the observed stacking pattern favor an in-plane moment orientation. These results reveal contrasting crystal-field and dipolar anisotropies in determining the magnetic ground state of NaBaEr(BO$_3$)$_2$.

papers.title: Neural Network Fractional Quantum Hall States with Learnable Orbital Pair Matrix Factors: Balancing Physical Priors and Flexibility
papers.abstract: Neural network fractional quantum Hall (FQH) states offer a promising alternative for capturing Landau level (LL) mixing and for understanding FQH physics, yet the incorporation of physical priors has so far been limited to the minimal exact constraints built into the ansatz. Working in spherical geometry, we show that the network's flexibility suffers both when only minimal additional physical priors are supplied and when priors such as flux attachment are imposed rigidly. In the former case, the monopole harmonic product orbital (MHPO) ansatz is difficult to optimize, whereas in the latter, the expressivity of the neural network is restricted. We therefore propose the orbital pair matrix factor MHPO (MHPO-M) ansatz, which balances physical priors against flexibility by not only replacing the fixed Laughlin structure with learnable pair factors but also making them dependent on both the electron configurations and the orbitals. Across $\nu=1/5$, $1/3$, and $2/5$, MHPO-M achieves the lowest variational energy among the tested variants, and a factorized orbital readout based on it enables scaling to 35 electrons, with energies competitive with trends inferred from three-LL exact-diagonalization results. These results demonstrate that physical priors can be appropriately incorporated without sacrificing the flexibility of neural network wavefunctions, opening a promising path toward accurate, scalable modeling of FQH systems with LL mixing.

papers.title: Floquet ground state order
papers.abstract: Clean, interacting, periodically driven systems are believed to thermalize to featureless, infinite-temperature states that preclude the formation of stable ordered states. Here, we show stable quantum order, distinct from prethermal order, and its phase transitions in the ground state of the average-energy operator. Decomposing the time evolution into geometric and average-energy dynamics, we apply Geometric Floquet theory to identify the Floquet ground state. We derive a general variational principle to compute the Floquet ground state in large interacting periodically driven systems, and use it to develop a matrix product state algorithm. In driven nonintegrable chains of more than 100 interacting spins, our numerical simulations exhibit a gapped, area-law entangled Floquet ground state in extended parameter regimes; the ground-state manifold can support both dressed equilibrium order (e.g., Floquet antiferromagnets) and inherently nonequilibrium order (e.g., ground-state time crystals). This quantum order is protected by a finite average-energy gap, which closes at phase transition points upon changing model parameters. We decompose Floquet phases of matter into their equilibrium and nonequilibrium elements: whereas the Floquet ground state at any fixed time is a representative of an equilibrium phase of matter, the nonequilibrium content is entirely produced by the drive holonomy and is geometric. Finally, we identify quasilocal counterdiabatic driving as a mechanism for the stability against heating of gapped Floquet ground states in nonintegrable quantum systems, and argue why Floquet ground states evade the Eigenstate Thermalization Hypothesis. Our work enables the study of interacting nonequilibrium matter deep into the many-body regime, and lays the foundations for the engineering of strongly correlated ordered quantum states.

papers.title: Quantum Spin Singlet Ground State with Large Excitation Gap in the S = 3/2 quasi-1D van der Waals materials MoX3 (X = I, Br)
papers.abstract: We report the first experimental evidence for a quantum-disordered spin-singlet ground state and gapped triplon excitations in quasi-one-dimensional van der Waals materials. The insulating van der Waals trihalides MoI3 and MoBr3 are analyzed in a combined thermodynamic, spectroscopic, and theoretical investigation. These materials contain structurally dimerized atomic chains of face-sharing octahedra with alternating short and long Mo-Mo separations along the chain direction. Temperature-dependent bulk magnetic susceptibility measurements reveal a broad thermally activated response consistent with a large spin gap. Inelastic neutron scattering (INS) spectra provide direct evidence of a collective spin gap at an exceptionally large energy transfer of ~ 30 meV (~ 348 K) for MoBr3. The absence of low-energy magnetic spectral weight and the activated susceptibility are inconsistent with a conventional classical antiferromagnetic ground state. Instead, they point to a spin-singlet ground state with a large singlet-triplet excitation gap. To identify the microscopic origin of this gap, we perform density matrix renormalization group (DMRG) calculations on one-dimensional spin chains using exchange constants derived from density functional theory (DFT). The dominance of the single dimer exchange term allows the inter-dimer coupling along the chain and between chains to be treated using perturbation theory. Intrachain exchange lowers the isolated-dimer triplet energy by producing a dispersive triplon band. INS data show the triplon bandwidth to be ~ 20 meV. Interchain coupling produces negligible additional bandwidth on the order of 1 meV. The INS measurements directly establish quantum spin-singlet and triplon physics in MoBr3 with a large singlet-triplet gap on the scale of room temperature, while the susceptibility and theoretical results indicate closely analogous behavior in MoI3.

papers.title: Theoretical Description of Electronic Modulation and Superconducting Coherence
papers.abstract: An electronic modulation can retain a substantial local amplitude while its translational coherence is limited by spatial disorder. Its coupling to superconductivity therefore cannot be characterized by a single modulation intensity. We develop a phenomenological formulation of a finite-wave-vector complex electronic envelope coupled to a charged superconducting field. Translation and gauge symmetries constrain the interaction terms, while amplitude, modulation-gradient and condensate-gradient couplings act on distinct responses. The resulting variational equations give uniform coexistence conditions, local stability criteria and phase-gradient coefficients. We define the helicity modulus by a boundary twist, distinguish phase-only from amplitude-weighted correlations, and give an explicit minimal spectral Hamiltonian illustrating how the electronic texture may enter momentum-resolved measurements. The proposed tests use distinct spatial, spectral and stiffness observables; none assumes that a tunnelling gap directly measures condensate amplitude. An explicit kernel expansion yields the leading displacement of the selected wave vector, while the thermodynamic twist response determines phase rigidity independently of charge intensity. The analytical relations and selected numerical responses distinguish amplitude, spatial organization and condensate rigidity within the specified coupled-field model.

papers.title: Topological Charge-2ne Superconductivity and Clustering Hierarchy
papers.abstract: Charge-$2ne$ superconductors condense clusters of more than two electrons, extending superconductivity beyond Cooper pairing. They exhibit distinctive signatures including fractional flux quantization $h/(2ne)$ and are actively being explored in strongly correlated systems. We develop a general framework for constructing and characterizing \emph{topological} charge-$2ne$ superconductors by combining wavefunction and field theory approaches. Generalizing the Read-Green wavefunction and Higgsing Read-Rezayi-type states yield two families that can support deconfined non-Abelian anyons and non-Abelian superconducting vortices. The first family also admits a construction from doping Jain states. Through Higgs theories, we find that the first and second families realize weak and intermediate clustering regimes, respectively, distinguished by the topology of vortices carrying flux greater than $h/(2ne)$, while strong clustering yields a charge-$2ne$ superconductor without intrinsic topological order. These reveal that higher-charge superconductivity supports a richer hierarchy of topological phases beyond the Read-Green weak-strong pairing dichotomy, with distinct internal clustering structures giving rise to different topological structures at fixed condensate charge.

papers.title: Field Theory of the Gutzwiller Projection
papers.abstract: The Gutzwiller projection produces a well-known ansatz for spin-liquid and quantum Hall ground-state wavefunctions that is amenable to numerical simulation, with the Laughlin wavefunction being the most celebrated example. A long-standing issue is the precise relation between the Gutzwiller projection and the closely related parton gauge theory. Here, we clarify this issue by providing a field-theoretic description of the Gutzwiller projection. In a path integral description, the universal physics of the projected state is described in terms of a gauge field supported on a temporal slab of vanishing width $\epsilon \rightarrow 0$ coupled to the bulk matter fields. We analytically derive the universal physics of various Gutzwiller projected states. Our construction is also applicable to discrete symmetries, and we use it to analyze various projected SPT states. Among our results, we show that the Gutzwiller projection is not a good ansatz for the long-distance properties of $U(1)$ Dirac spin liquids, spinon Fermi surface spin liquids or composite Fermi liquids, and that the Gutzwiller projection of a quantum spin Hall state has only quasi-long range order. In contrast, in examples where the gauge field is gapped, including Laughlin states, $\mathbb{Z}_2$ spin liquids and Luttinger liquids, we show that the slab gauge theory from Gutzwiller projection reproduces the correct universal physics of the full parton gauge theory. We also present a generalization of our field theory that describes $G$-intertwining defects, with application to self-duality defects of recent theoretical interest.

papers.title: Spectral signatures of hidden order and hidden quantum critical points
papers.abstract: Hidden-order phases elude the conventional Ginzburg-Landau framework: although they spontaneously break symmetry, their order remains invisible to standard local two-point correlators. Instead, they are typically characterized by nonlocal (string) order parameters and are believed to underlie a range of exotic quantum states, such as symmetry-protected topological (SPT) phases. While hidden correlations have previously been detected through nonlocal observables in quantum gas microscope experiments, in realistic solid-state systems multipoint observables are typically inaccessible and the signatures of hidden order remain largely unexplored. In this work, we show that hidden order in doped spin chains can be directly probed through dynamical two-point response functions measurable by resonant inelastic X-ray scattering (RIXS) and neutron scattering. Focusing on a minimal model, we numerically identify clear spectral fingerprints of both the hidden-order phase, its associated hidden quantum critical point as well as a specific group of gapless SPT phases. Complementing our numerical results with analytical insights, we uncover the microscopic origin of these spectral signatures and demonstrate how they emerge from the interplay between spin and charge degrees of freedom. Together, our results establish spectroscopy as a practical probe of hidden order and gapless SPT phases and provide a unified understanding of the low-energy physics governing these unconventional quantum phases.

papers.title: Finite-temperature spectral functions of lattice polarons with process tensors
papers.abstract: We develop a process tensor approach for calculating the finite-temperature spectral functions of lattice polarons. We show that the finite-temperature phonon influence functional can be expressed as the elementwise exponential of a low-rank matrix product state, enabling an efficient summation of electron worldlines. An embedding construction embeds worldlines of different propagation times into a single matrix product state. This construction yields the propagator over the full simulated time interval in a single calculation. We benchmark this approach against available finite-temperature density-matrix renormalization group results for the one-dimensional Holstein polaron. We further obtain numerically converged spectra for the two-dimensional Holstein polaron. The spectra reveal a progressive transfer of spectral weight from coherent spectral features into an incoherent background with increasing temperature.

papers.title: Orbital Magnetization within Self-Consistent Hartree-Fock via an Envelope Theorem
papers.abstract: Orbital magnetization is an elementary thermodynamic response function of a quantum system: the derivative of the grand potential with respect to magnetic field. However, naive perturbation theory is fraught with difficulties, as even infinitesimal magnetic fields shatter any bands into a Hofstadter butterfly spectrum. Even at the self-consistent Hartree-Fock (mean field) level, rigorous formulas for the orbital magnetization have only become available within the last year. This work provides a straightforward derivation of orbital magnetization at the mean field level using a completely real-space approach. The key tools used are the magnetic perturbation theory developed in the 1960s and an envelope theorem, which is a standard result in the calculus of variations. For simplicity, we restrict to insulating states at zero temperature on the infinite plane. We also discuss the natural connections to projected position operators and quantum geometry, as well as practical numerical computations.

papers.title: Symmetry Enriched Criticality from Kennedy Tasaki Self-Duality
papers.abstract: The interplay between topology and quantum criticality has established symmetry enriched criticality as a new paradigm beyond conventional frameworks in condensed matter and statistical physics. However, the conditions under which such criticality emerges remain poorly understood. In this work, we show that a broad class of symmetry enriched critical points separating symmetry protected topological (SPT) and spontaneous symmetry breaking (SSB) phases is governed by Kennedy Tasaki (KT) self duality. At these criticalities, the KT transformation that interchanges the SPT and SSB phases acts as a self-dual noninvertible symmetry, endowing the critical points with nontrivial topological characteristics. We numerically demonstrate this mechanism in $\mathbb{Z}_{n} \times \mathbb{Z}_{n}$ cluster qudit chains and further argue that it naturally extends to higher dimensions, providing a duality based criterion for identifying symmetry-enriched criticality across dimensions.

papers.title: Spin fluctuations and nearly isotropic quasiparticles in the doped three-dimensional Hubbard model
papers.abstract: Away from half filling and above its Neel temperature, the three-dimensional Hubbard model is a paramagnetic metal with antiferromagnetic spin fluctuations, where controlled momentum-resolved results have been lacking. Using connected-determinant diagrammatic Monte Carlo, we compute the momentum-resolved self-energy for n = 0.4-0.95, T/t = 0.05-0.33 and U/t = 4-8, and the full-zone spin susceptibility at twelve of these points, focusing on U/t = 4. At U/t = 4 and toward half filling the spin fluctuations become strong: for n = 0.7-0.9 at T/t = 0.14 they enhance the susceptibility peak up to sevenfold and raise the momentum-dependent part of the scattering rate to four to five times its second-order value. They are driven by an effective spin interaction screened to about 2U/3 and nearly uniform over the zone. Yet the peak height is set by the slightly smaller value of this interaction at the peak wave vector, and near magnetic order this small difference changes the height by a large factor. Two-particle self-consistent theory reproduces the peak because its sum rule fixes its single constant interaction near this value, but for n = 0.7-0.9 at T/t = 0.14 its self-energy overestimates the local scattering rate and underestimates the momentum-dependent part. Though strong, the fluctuations are short ranged, with a correlation length of at most about two lattice spacings, and for n = 0.7-0.9 and T/t >= 0.14 the scattering rate near the Fermi surface varies by at most about 1% at fixed band energy, without hot spots. At U/t = 4 dynamical mean-field theory (DMFT) reproduces the local scattering rate and quasiparticle weight within a few percent, and the nonlocal part it misses is approximately a function of the band energy. Strong spin fluctuations thus coexist with nearly isotropic quasiparticles, and the results provide a benchmark for extensions of DMFT and for spin-fluctuation theories.

papers.title: Suppression and reemergence of directional transport across the ferromagnetic transition in SrRuO$_3$
papers.abstract: SrRuO$_3$ is a canonical itinerant ferromagnet that continues to serve as a fertile platform for exploring spin-orbit coupled transport and topological responses in correlated oxide metals. Here, we investigate a (110)-oriented epitaxial SrRuO3 thin film on DyScO$_3$, where crystallographic anisotropy allows for symmetry-resolved charge transport along orthogonal in-plane directions. We uncover two principal findings. First, the resistance above the Curie temperature $T_{c,on}\approx 165$ K exhibits strong anisotropy, consistent with directionally dependent spin-fluctuation scattering. Below $T_{c,on}$, this anisotropy nearly vanishes, despite persistent structural inequivalence, due to isotropic electron-magnon and electron-electron scattering processes. Second, the application of a magnetic field reveals a striking directional contrast in the linear magnetoresistance (MR): it remains negative and saturates along [001], but changes sign and becomes positive along $[1\bar{1}0]$ below $T_0=145$ K. In contrast, the quadratic MR term is identical for both directions and peaks near $T_{\mathrm{OHE}}^*=155$ K, where the ordinary Hall coefficient crosses zero, consistent with carrier compensation under a two-band scenario. A sign change in the anomalous Hall signal at $T_{\mathrm{AHE}}^*=150$ K is consistent with a temperature-dependent redistribution of Berry-curvature contributions near the Fermi level. These results establish ferromagnetic ordering as the primary driver of the observed directional magnetotransport in SrRuO$_3$.

papers.title: Field theories and critical excitations at anyon condensation transitions
papers.abstract: Anyon condensation transitions remain challenging to characterize especially when the condensing anyons are non-abelian. We develop two complementary approaches for extracting information about the transition from the categorical data of the parent topological order and the condensate. The first adapts a Ginzburg-Landau procedure developed for $1+1$D transitions in the SymTFT setting to $2+1$D anyon condensation transitions. The construction applies when the anyons participating in the condensate have integer quantum dimensions. The second gives a criterion for identifying which point and loop excitations become critical at a continuous transition. The key step is to determine which anyon loops remain condensed throughout. All other loops become critical, while a point excitation becomes critical if it braids trivially with every condensed loop. We illustrate both proposals in several abelian and non-abelian examples.

papers.title: Classical spin liquids in the kagome Ising model, and their link with magnetoelasticity
papers.abstract: We investigate a nearest-neighbor Ising model on the kagome lattice coupled to elastic lattice distortions. By integrating out the lattice degrees of freedom, we derive an approximate spin-only description in terms of a kagome \(J_1\)-\(J_2\)-\(J_{3}\) Ising model with interactions extending to third nearest-neighbors. Using tensor network methods complemented by classical Monte Carlo simulations, we revisit its zero-temperature phase diagram and characterize the ground states studied more than thirty years ago. We discover three phases with extensive zero-temperature entropy and algebraically decaying spin correlations. Importantly, these states are not confined to fine-tuned points or frontiers between phases, but occupy extended areas of parameter space. Their quasi long-range order is reflected in Bragg-like peaks in the structure factors; we relate this, and other properties, to diverse phases found in Ising and Heisenberg models. Finally, we trace the trajectories generated by the magnetoelastic coupling through the effective-model phase diagram, explaining the emergence of self-frustration for the unfrustrated magnetoelastic model with ferromagnetic interactions.

papers.title: Sum-over-poles framework for quantum embedding to approach the real-frequency axis
papers.abstract: We introduce a real-frequency framework for the quantum embedding of solids, based on sum-over-poles (SOP) representations. We partition the lattice into periodically repeated interacting fragments and derive an embedded Dyson equation for the fragment, to be solved self-consistently. The resulting scheme generalizes the algorithmic-inversion method of our previous work to interacting Hamiltonians and is closely related to dynamical mean-field theory (DMFT), especially when an extended impurity problem is introduced. By exploiting the compact pole expansion of the embedding potential, we carry out the self-consistent procedure close to the real axis, which avoids ill-posed analytic continuation. In addition, the SOP representation allows us to introduce a pole-and-residue dynamics, which we use to reach the self-consistent solution. After deriving the method, we benchmark it against exact-diagonalization implementations of DMFT on the one-dimensional Hubbard ring at half filling. The framework offers a natural route to real-space dynamical quantum embedding, for periodic systems as well as for strongly correlated defects in materials.

papers.title: Acceleration of CTQMC via Denoising Diffusion Models with Auxiliary Spectral Functions
papers.abstract: Continuous-time Quantum Monte Carlo (CTQMC) impurity solvers are a numerically exact, but expensive, option for solving the Dynamical Mean Field Theory (DMFT) equations, with statistical noise from undersampling presenting a major challenge to low temperature studies. This noise is especially egregious within the sampled self-energy, which can destabilize the self-consistency loop upon insertion into the Dyson equation. In this work, we introduce a neural denoiser for fermionic imaginary time Green's functions based on the diffusion model architecture trained on synthetic data. The network predicts positive and normalized auxiliary spectral functions consistent with the noisy imaginary axis CTQMC data, which is then refined via autodifferentiation to match the measured self-energy, its first two high-frequency moments, and impurity occupation similar to the Constrained Residual Minimization (CRM) method. This leads to Green's functions and self-energies that are causal by design. Through this denoising framework we are able to reduce the required CTQMC measurement steps by a factor of 10-100. We benchmark our method with a half-filled Hubbard model on a Bethe lattice, a two-patch Dynamical Cluster Approximation (DCA) of the two-dimensional Hubbard model, and the SrVO$_3$ system. We reproduce the Mott transition upon increasing Coulomb interaction for the half-filled Hubbard model with only 5000 CTQMC measurements, the pseudogap transition for the DCA two-dimensional Hubbard model with only 5$\times$10$^5$ measurements, and match the spectral function of SrVO$_3$ with 50 times fewer measurements than the reference. Since we generate auxiliary spectral functions, we recover the approximate spectral functions of the systems for free without performing analytic continuation.
